advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the present-only key contract in resolve_project() with the reducer now always seeding `bridge_project: None`, so legacy tickets still resolve to legacy_default.
evidence: ABSENCE: `search_files` for `resolve_project` finds only its definition and tests — no wired caller yet, so this is a latent contract mismatch, not an active break, but it will bite when the inbound/outbound sync stories consume reduced state.
advisory.finding: The reducer now seeds `bridge_project: None` into every ticket's initial state, so a reduced state dict ALWAYS contains the `bridge_project` key. The existing consumer `projects_store.resolve_project()` distinguishes the legacy/absent state via key-absence (`if "bridge_project" not in ticket: return mapping.legacy_default`). When resolve_project is fed a reduced state, that absent-key branch is unreachable and a legacy ticket (bridge_project None) falls through to `if not value: return None`, resolving to never-sync instead of legacy_default — a semantic mismatch between how state is projected and how it is consumed.
scenarios: A legacy ticket (created before this change, no bridge_project in CREATE data) is reduced to `bridge_project: None`, then handed to resolve_project once sync is wired — it returns None (never-sync) rather than the configured legacy_default.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make CREATE `_apply_bridge_repos` str()-coerce list repos items to match the EDIT path and the string-item schema.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:99:             else [r for r in repos if r]
src/rebar/_commands/composer_edit.py: "else [str(r) for r in (raw_value or []) if r]"
advisory.finding: CREATE's `_apply_bridge_repos` does not str()-coerce list items for `repos` (`[r for r in repos if r]`), whereas EDIT's `_edit_repos_list` does (`[str(r) for r in (raw_value or []) if r]`). A library/MCP create passing non-string repos items would store non-strings, violating the schema's `items: {type: string}`, while the EDIT path would coerce them.
scenarios: A programmatic caller passing repos=[1, 2] to create_ticket stores ints in the CREATE event, whereas the same via edit would be coerced to strings.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `--bridge-project=VALUE` and `--repos=VALUE` to `_EDIT_USAGE` so the printed edit usage matches the documented and accepted flags.
evidence: edit_cli prints this string on the argv<2 path: `print(_EDIT_USAGE, file=sys.stderr)`
advisory.finding: The operator-facing `_EDIT_USAGE` string printed on `edit` error still omits `--bridge-project` and `--repos`, contradicting the edit help/reference which now document these flags as accepted.
advisory.suggested_fix: Insert `[--bridge-project=VALUE] [--repos=VALUE]` into `_EDIT_USAGE` alongside the tag flags to match edit.txt.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that edits `--repos` on an existing ticket (CSV string and list forms) and asserts the reduced `repos` state after replay.
evidence: Only edit calls in the suite are `--bridge-project` (tests/unit/test_ticket_project_fields.py:183,191); grep for `edit` finds no `--repos` edit.
New EDIT-only helper `_edit_repos_list` at src/rebar/_commands/composer_edit.py:71-82 with distinct CSV/list logic not covered by the CREATE tests.
EDIT projection path src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:361-375 (`process_edit` merges fields into state) is unexercised for `repos`.
Docs assert edit behavior: 'Bridge project: ... --repos replaces the associated repositories (CSV) and is freely editable.' (src/rebar/_cli/help/edit.txt)
advisory.finding: No test exercises the EDIT `--repos` path. `repos` is documented as a freely-editable EDIT field, has its own normalization helper `_edit_repos_list` (CSV split, list coercion, None-tolerance) distinct from the CREATE path, and projects through `process_edit`, yet every test that touches `repos` sets it at CREATE only. A regression in EDIT-time repos normalization or projection (e.g. failing to split a CSV string, or stringifying a list into its repr) would pass all tests.
scenarios: An implementer breaks `_edit_repos_list` CSV splitting or list-repr coercion; suite stays green.
EDIT sets repos to a new CSV and the reducer fails to project it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_edit_repos_replaces_after_replay`: create a ticket with repos=['a'], run `rebar edit <id> --repos b,c`, assert `_state(...)['repos'] == ['b','c']`; also cover the library `edit(repos=[...])` path.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that edits an unbound ticket to `--bridge-project ""` and asserts the reduced state projects `""` (not None) after replay.
evidence: Docs: 'Bridge project: --bridge-project is promote-only — it may be set on an UNBOUND ticket ...; "" marks never-sync.' (src/rebar/_cli/help/edit.txt)
CREATE three-state test exists (test_three_states_are_distinguishable_after_replay:108) but has no EDIT analogue for the "" never-sync promotion.
advisory.finding: The EDIT contract documents `"" marks never-sync` for --bridge-project (an unbound ticket may be promoted to explicit never-sync), but no test edits bridge_project to an empty string. The promote-only test only sets/refuses 'REB'/'DIG', so the empty-string EDIT projection (distinct-falsy sentinel on the edit path, symmetric to the CREATE three-state test) is untested.
scenarios: An unbound ticket is edited with `--bridge-project ''` to mark never-sync; the empty-string projection on the EDIT path regresses (e.g. collapses to None) undetected.
